requirements.initial: A runtime home has one live or stale Guardian owner.
requirements.action: Acquire or explicitly take over its lock.
requirements.expected: A live owner remains authoritative and only one replacement wins.

evidence.assertion: refuses a second live owner without takeover
evidence.scope: Real temporary filesystem lock state with FakeProcesses liveness/signals; no OS owner processes.

evidence.assertion: allows only one concurrent contender to replace a stale owner
evidence.scope: Concurrent in-process lock contenders with real filesystem writes and FakeProcesses; no OS process contention.

evidence.assertion: keeps a live owner authoritative even when its heartbeat is stale
evidence.scope: Real temporary lock files; FakeProcesses liveness, no OS ownership.

evidence.assertion: treats a reused pid as stale without killing the unrelated process
evidence.scope: Real temporary lock files; injected PID start identities/signals.

evidence.assertion: falls back to SIGKILL when the owner ignores graceful shutdown
evidence.scope: Temporary lock state; FakeProcesses signals and waits, separate from real subprocess cleanup.

requirements.gap: Real multi-process owner contention is not proved by these FakeProcesses specs. Compose source, packaged, and installed launchers under the same restart/cleanup acceptance.

requirements.initial: A test-owned child exits or an owner tree is retired.
requirements.expected: Required services recover and no owned process/port remains.

evidence.scope: Starts and kills test-owned Guardian trees.
UTA restart/orphan-port subchecks are currently SOFT; green exit is not proof of those subchecks.

evidence.assertion: retries forever with capped backoff and resets after recovery
evidence.scope: Fake timers and controlled recovery results; proves scheduling/reset only, no real service recovery.

requirements.gap: Stage 2 must distinguish required versus advisory subchecks and record individual failure/cleanup outcomes.

requirements.initial: The control socket disappears but Alice ownership can remain.
requirements.action: Inspect status and stop through advertised capabilities.
requirements.expected: Remaining writer lock prevents absent status; unsupported stop is refused.

evidence.assertion: keeps shutdown non-absent while an Alice runtime lock is still active
uses capability rather than launcher surface to reject an unsupported stop
evidence.scope: Real local control socket and controlled status server; no owned Runtime process tree.

requirements.gap: Actual owner tree/port disappearance remains dedicated process acceptance.

requirements.initial: A wrapper owns a detached descendant.
requirements.action: Terminate owner tree while wrapper can exit first.
requirements.expected: Both process identities cease to be alive under current PID oracle.

evidence.assertion: terminates descendants even when the package-manager-like wrapper exits first
evidence.scope: Real Node subprocesses; OS reaper/zombie semantics are environment-sensitive.

evidence.assertion: cancels a pending recovery on stop

requirements.gap: Positive PID existence alone cannot distinguish exited zombies from executing descendants; corroborate OS state independently. Termination does not establish external-init reaping of orphan PID entries. Separate native process/port/lock completion, real service recovery, and multi-launcher contention remain unproved.

requirements.initial: A selected home is absent, starting, or already owned.
requirements.action: Start a Runtime and wait for readiness, or reject a racing owner.
requirements.expected: Readiness follows running status; ownership transitions remain Guardian-authorized and background CLI does not open a browser.

evidence.assertion: starts a detached Guardian and emits readiness as structured state
evidence.scope: Fake child/status sequence; verifies spawn options, unref/log closure and ready envelope, no native Guardian.

evidence.assertion: allows its spawned Guardian ownership transition but rejects a racing owner
evidence.scope: Controlled Runtime status and child; verifies EOWNED and retirement of the test-owned failed start.

evidence.assertion: preserves Guardian takeover authority instead of signaling the old owner itself
evidence.scope: Injected spawn/status; takeover env forwarded without CLI signaling the previous owner.

evidence.assertion: presents structured background readiness without opening a browser
evidence.scope: Injected lifecycle core; verifies CLI presentation and browser boundary, separate from core readiness and real launcher acceptance.

requirements.gap: Native packaged startup, real service readiness/port release, Windows/Bun/Electron and multi-launcher contention still require their dedicated acceptance.
